raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`--linear-backend conch` dies at the first forward pass on `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16`:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x30a2bea0) on address 0x7e69a4600000. Reason: Unknown.
```

48 of the model's layers are fused `in_proj_ba` projections with `N=96`. Conch's W4A16 kernel loads the weight block and the per-group scales in 64-column tiles with no bounds mask, so the second tile covers columns 96-127: **128 B of packed weight and 64 B of scales per row past the end of the buffer**.

This PR handles those shapes in vLLM's Conch wrapper: a `K` the kernel cannot address is refused, and `N` is padded up to the kernel's tile width. All 48 layers then load and run - decode TPOT **-31.7% / -29.4% / -22.5%** vs the default Triton kernel at c=1/8/32 (8k-in / 1k-out). Selection is untouched: Triton stays the default, Conch stays opt-in, and conch
itself is not patched.

The change is shape arithmetic in the wrapper rather than anything platform-specific, so it should hold for any conch-enabled target; validated on `gfx950` (MI355X).

## Claims

* **Refuse the K side.** Every kernel implements `can_implement`, the hook vLLM calls to ask "can you run this layer?". `ConchLinearKernel.can_implement` now says no when the input dimension `K` is not a multiple of the kernel's 64-wide tile, or not a multiple of the quantization group size; channelwise layers (`group_size == -1`, one scale per output column) are checked as if the group size were `K`. None of this model's `K` values (5120, 6144, 17408) trip these, so the checks do not fire here - they stop another model from reaching the kernel with a `K` it mis-addresses.
* **Pad the N side.** Refusing works for `K` but not for `N`: with `uint8b128` weights and bf16 activations Conch is the only kernel available on ROCm (Triton supports only 4-bit weight types, Exllama needs fp16 activations), so refusing a non-multiple `N` would make those layers unloadable. Instead the packed weights, their scales and their zero points are zero-extended along `N` to the kernel's tile width, and the extra output columns are dropped before the bias is added - `N=96` becomes 128 that way. The pad is taken from the unpacked launch-layout weight, so `N` must be a whole number of packing groups (8 for 4-bit); a partial group is refused at selection. This checkpoint has no `uint8b128` layers.
* **Refuse to serve stale weights after a reload.** The pad cache is derived state, and the layerwise reload path re-registers the pre-reload buffers while its captured metadata (recorded at model construction, before any pads exist) has no pads at all - so a reloaded padded layer would keep the old weights in its pads while the parameters get the new ones. Reprocessing a padded layer now raises with an actionable message. The check keys on a plain attribute rather than on the buffers, precisely because the reload deletes every registered tensor before it re-runs this method. Not covered: a reload that supplies weights already in kernel format (`is_checkpoint_format=False`), which skips weight processing entirely and so cannot be detected from inside the kernel; that combination is documented as unsupported.
* All 48 `N=96` layers load (`Using ConchLinearKernel for mixed-precision linear`), 0 memory faults.
* Decode TPOT **-31.7% / -29.4% / -22.5%** at 8k-in / 1k-out, c=1/8/32; our own A/B/B/A harness on short prompts gives **-38.1% / -37.7% / -36.6%** (method in the collapsible below). Prefill is slower - see the note under the bench table.
* Greedy 4/4 byte-identical between backends; gsm8k equal to the last reported digit.


## Validation

serving command, the two arms differ only by the flag:

```
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16 \
  --served-model-name qwen38-int4 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --seed 42 [--linear-backend conch]
```

bench serve command, c=1/8/32 (means, one run per cell):

```
vllm bench serve --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model qwen38-int4 \
  --tokenizer amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.0 --seed 42 \
  --num-prompts {8,16,32} --max-concurrency {1,8,32}
```

| c | TTFT ms triton -> conch | TPOT ms triton -> conch | output tok/s triton -> conch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 908.4 -> 1240.8 (+36.6%) | 91.25 -> **62.30** (-31.7%) | 10.9 -> 15.8 (+45.1%) |
| 8 | 5253.6 -> 6698.1 (+27.5%) | 95.31 -> **67.25** (-29.4%) | 79.6 -> 108.4 (+36.1%) |
| 32 | 17926.5 -> 23007.2 (+28.3%) | 110.41 -> **85.57** (-22.5%) | 249.0 -> 295.1 (+18.5%) |

> Prefill is slower with Conch. Decode dominates an 8k/1k request, so end to end Conch is still ahead there (65.0 s vs 94.4 s at c=1, computed as TTFT + 1023 x TPOT), but prefill-heavy or short-completion workloads should stay on Triton - which is why Conch stays opt-in.

<details>
<summary>Decode TPOT, custom bench (A/B/B/A, two boots per arm)</summary>

Method: four server runs in A/B/B/A order (Triton, Conch, Conch, Triton), one backend per run, 128-in/256-out random prompts, 16/32/64 requests per cell at c=1/8/32, 256 generated tokens, p50 per boot; the cells are symmetric so the two boots of the same backend also bound run-to-run noise (p50 spread <= 0.03 ms for Triton, <= 0.44 ms for Conch). The same runs produced the greedy outputs used for the byte-identical check. Re-checked on the final revision: 46.98 / 47.78 / 49.53 ms, i.e. unchanged within noise.

| concurrency | 1 | 8 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| triton | 75.91 | 76.55 | 78.18 |
| conch | 46.97 | 47.66 | 49.56 |
| delta | -38.1% | -37.7% | -36.6% |

</details>

`lm_eval`, gsm8k 25-shot, chat template, n=1319, 0 error rows:

```
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=qwen38-int4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=8000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":4096,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template
```

| arm | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.9704 +- 0.0047 | 0.9037 +- 0.0081 |
| conch | 0.9704 +- 0.0047 | 0.9037 +- 0.0081 |

Tests: `44 passed, 24 skipped` (gfx950) over the five quantization test files;
`pre-commit` passes on the two changed files. 

New coverage, all behavioural (real kernel, or the real reload entry points):

* `can_implement`: which shapes it refuses and why, the explicit-backend failure path, and `uint8b128` selection.
* Numerics against hand-computed dequantized references: symmetric `N=96` padding (bit-identical to a tile-aligned `N=64` layer), asymmetric zero-point padding (width and strides), and channelwise `group_size == -1`.
* Reload: driven through `record_metadata_for_reloading` and `initialize_layerwise_reload`, then a padded layer must refuse reprocessing.



## Details

The two loads that feed the tile in `conch/kernels/quantization/gemm.py` - the weight block and the per-group scales - are plain `tl.load`s with no bounds mask, unlike the masked loads and the masked output store next to them. With `N=96` the second 64-column tile reads columns 96-127, past the end of each row of packed weights and scales. If the following page is unmapped that faults (what we first saw); if it is mapped the read is silently out of bounds, and because the tail columns are masked at store time the results stayed correct in that case. A `K` that is not a multiple of the group size walks the scale buffer the same way, which is why the K side is refused rather than padded.

The fix is on our side because conch is pinned (`conch-triton-kernels==1.2.1`), its repository has been quiet since 2025-10-02, and the same unguarded code is in the 1.3 wheel. 

Notes:

* The pads live in three non-persistent buffers (each a tensor or `None`): out of `state_dict()`, moved by `Module.to()` / `Module.cpu()`, and kept at a stable address so CUDA graph replay reads them. That stable address is also why a reload cannot refresh them - see the guard above. Registered parameters keep their original shapes.
* The tile width is read from the kernel at first use rather than hard-coded. If that private helper disappears we fall back to conch 1.2.1's 64 x 64, which would silently under-pad if a future conch used wider tiles.
* A `uint8b128` layer whose `K` Conch cannot address is now unselectable (fails at selection with the reason) instead of being accepted and faulting at runtime.
* The reload gap is general, not conch-specific: registering a buffer does not make a layerwise reload refresh it (the reload restores the pre-reload captured allocation). It is tracked in the stable-runtime-tensor RFC (#57895) and being migrated kernel by kernel (#59000); until that lands, a padded layer refuses.



---

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,409 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for the Conch W4A16 mixed-precision kernel (ROCm).
+
+Covers can_implement's tile preconditions, the raise for an explicit
+--linear-backend that cannot implement a shape, auto-selection, and numerics
+with the padded-N weight cache.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear as linear_kernels_pkg
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear import (
+    MPLinearLayerConfig,
+    choose_mp_linear_kernel,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mixed_precision.conch import (
+    ConchLinearKernel,
+    _conch_padded_width,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.scalar_type import scalar_types
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
+# This test module is ROCm/Conch specific. Avoid import-time failures on
+# non-ROCm or environments without conch by skipping early.
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    pytest.skip("ROCm only", allow_module_level=True)
+
+pytest.importorskip("conch")
+
+device = "cuda"
+
+
+def _make_config(
+    K: int,
+    N: int,
+    group_size: int,
+    weight_type=scalar_types.uint4b8,
+    act_type=torch.bfloat16,
+    zero_points: bool = False,
+) -> MPLinearLayerConfig:
+    return MPLinearLayerConfig(
+        full_weight_shape=(K, N),
+        partition_weight_shape=(K, N),
+        weight_type=weight_type,
+        act_type=act_type,
+        group_size=group_size,
+        zero_points=zero_points,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "K,N,group_size,expected,reason_substr",
+    [
+        (5120, 16384, 128, True, ""),
+        # N=96 (issue-60581): padded up in process_weights_after_loading, so accept it.
+        (5120, 96, 128, True, ""),
+        # A partial packing group cannot be padded (the unpacked weight is ceil-packed).
+        (5120, 100, 128, False, "packing"),
+        # K-side violations cannot be padded away.
+        (192, 1024, 128, False, "group size"),  # K % gs != 0
+        (196, 1024, 128, False, "block_k"),  # K % block_k != 0
+        # Channelwise: gs resolves to K, which is tile-aligned here.
+        (5120, 16384, -1, True, ""),
+    ],
+)
+def test_conch_can_implement_matrix(K, N, group_size, expected, reason_substr):
+    config = _make_config(K, N, group_size)
+    can_implement, reason = ConchLinearKernel.can_implement(config)
+    assert can_implement is expected
+    if not expected:
+        assert reason is not None and reason_substr in reason
+
+
+def test_explicit_backend_raises_for_unimplementable_shape(monkeypatch):
+    """--linear-backend conch + K=196 (rejected by conch) raises ValueError with
+    the rejection reason instead of silently running another backend."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(linear_kernels_pkg, "_get_linear_backend", lambda **_: "conch")
+    config = _make_config(196, 96, 128)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
+        choose_mp_linear_kernel(config)
+
+    message = str(excinfo.value)
+    assert "WNA16 linear layer" in message
+    assert "ConchLinearKernel" in message
+    assert "must be divisible" in message
+
+
+def test_auto_backend_still_raises_when_nothing_implements(monkeypatch):
+    """With backend "auto" nothing falls back: every real kernel rejects K=196,
+    so selection still raises ValueError listing the per-kernel reasons."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(linear_kernels_pkg, "_get_linear_backend", lambda **_: "auto")
+    config = _make_config(196, 96, 128)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
+        choose_mp_linear_kernel(config)
+
+    message = str(excinfo.value)
+    assert "WNA16 linear layer" in message
+    assert "TritonW4A16LinearKernel" in message
+    assert "ConchLinearKernel" in message
+
+
+def test_uint8b128_auto_selects_conch():
+    # triton supports only 4-bit weights and exllama needs fp16 activations, so
+    # Conch is the only candidate for uint8b128 + bf16 (N=96 pads up).
+    config = _make_config(
+        5120, 96, 128, weight_type=scalar_types.uint8b128, zero_points=False
+    )
+    assert choose_mp_linear_kernel(config) is ConchLinearKernel
+
+
+def _build_quark_layer(
+    monkeypatch, K, N, w_ckpt_kn8, scale_gn, zp_ckpt=None, process=True
+):
+    """A real QuarkW4A16Int4 layer (parameters + process sequence) wired to
+    ConchLinearKernel with random packed checkpoint data; zp_ckpt, if given, is
+    the asymmetric zero point in Quark's packed layout."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.quark.schemes import (
+        quark_w4a16_int4 as quark_w4a16_int4_module,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.quark.schemes.quark_w4a16_int4 import (
+        QuarkW4A16Int4,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
+        kInt4Static,
+        kInt4StaticAsym,
+    )
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        quark_w4a16_int4_module,
+        "choose_mp_linear_kernel",
+        lambda config, compute_capability=None: ConchLinearKernel,
+    )
+
+    scheme = QuarkW4A16Int4(
+        weight_quant_key=kInt4Static if zp_ckpt is None else kInt4StaticAsym,
+        activation_quant_key=None,
+        pack_method="reorder",
+        weight_config={"group_size": 128, "symmetric": zp_ckpt is None},
+    )
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    # The scheme locks in the kernel config before weights exist.
+    assert scheme.group_size == 128
+    assert scheme.is_symmetric == (zp_ckpt is None)
+    scheme.create_weights(
+        layer=layer,
+        output_partition_sizes=[N],
+        input_size_per_partition=K,
+        params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        weight_loader=lambda *args, **kwargs: None,
+        input_size=K,
+        output_size=N,
+    )
+    layer.weight.data = w_ckpt_kn8
+    layer.weight_scale.data = scale_gn
+    if zp_ckpt is not None:
+        layer.weight_zero_point.data = zp_ckpt
+    if process:
+        scheme.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+    return scheme, layer

+def _quark_reference(x, w_q_kn8, scale_gn, *, group_size, weight_bias, zp_gn=None):
+    """fp32 dequant reference reading the POST-transform [K/8, N] nibbles:
+    nibble at shift 4*(k%8), minus weight_bias (or the per-group zero points),
+    times scale[k//gs, n]."""
+    K, N = x.shape[1], w_q_kn8.shape[1]
+    shifts = torch.arange(8, device=w_q_kn8.device, dtype=torch.int32) * 4
+    nibbles = ((w_q_kn8.unsqueeze(-1) >> shifts) & 0xF).permute(0, 2, 1)
+    w_fp = nibbles.reshape(K, N).to(torch.float32)
+    if zp_gn is not None:
+        w_fp = w_fp - zp_gn.to(torch.float32).repeat_interleave(group_size, dim=0)
+    else:
+        w_fp = w_fp - weight_bias
+    w_fp = w_fp * scale_gn.to(torch.float32).repeat_interleave(group_size, dim=0)
+    return (x.to(torch.float32) @ w_fp).to(x.dtype)
